pr.title: Note every other state a pull request's row could show, and spell the holds out in an open drawer
pr.head: 8f359a0209f48486c91e4d5d0fa07c4b8de478d6

summary: Projector's Claude Code mod draws a panel above the prompt with one line for each pull request the session fixes or reviews. Each line shows the pull request's number, one state word, the title, a few notes after the title, and an age. The state is the most urgent thing that applies, taken in a fixed order: conflict, failing, changes, threads, reviewing, clean, then draft or ready.

Before this change the notes named only the holds that the state had not already named. A hold is something that keeps the pull request from merging: a conflict, failing checks, a change request, or open review threads. The two labels a review sets, reviewing and clean, never showed as notes. So a signed-off pull request whose checks failed read failing, and nothing on its line showed that it still carried clean.

Now the notes name every other state that applies, in the state's order and each in its own color: failing and changes in short, then the reviewing and clean labels, then approved, then the open threads' count, such as 2*. A conflict always takes the state, so no note names it. While a pull request's drawer is open, its line spells the holds out as checks failing and changes requested, and also names the hold that is already the state.

cards.html:

groups.title: Which notes a row shows
groups.kicker: The rule that picks a row's notes, and the open-drawer wording
intro: All of the change's logic is in hooks/register.tsx. HOLDS is the table of holds, most urgent first, and rowState picks the line's state word from it, then from the review labels. notesOf builds the notes after the title, and now takes whether the row's drawer is open.

Each hold now carries a phrase, its full wording, in place of the old note. Only failing and changes have one. A hold with no phrase never becomes a note: conflict, because it always wins the state, and threads, because its count is always a note of its own. The review labels move into a table, REVIEW_LABELS, that both rowState and notesOf read, so the two agree on the labels' order and colors.

checks.text: A note's color comes from the same HOLDS or REVIEW_LABELS entry that colors the state word, so a red or yellow note always matches the color that hold would get as the state. The collapsed line, which shows only numbers in statusColor, is unchanged.

files.note: notesOf now lists every hold and review label that applies, except the one that is the row's state, and spells the holds out while the drawer is open.

checks.text: A closed row leaves out the hold that is its state, and an open row keeps it in its full wording. The isOpen || status !== shown test is the whole difference between the two.

A review label becomes a note only when a hold, or reviewing, took the state, because otherwise reviewLabel makes that label the state. So a running review over an earlier clean reads reviewing with a clean note.

A loading row stays muted with no notes. Its placeholder from loadingOf in hooks/github.ts has no labels, no review decision, no threads, and no checks, so notesOf returns nothing for it. Checked by reading both functions.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: The panel test that pins the rule, and the user guide's description of it
intro: The rewritten panel test reads the notes of five rows with every drawer closed, then opens two drawers and reads them again. It compares whole note lists, each part with its color, so a missing note, a repeated state, or the wrong open-drawer wording turns it red. A new fixture, p21, is a signed-off pull request whose checks fail.
docs/plugins.md is the user guide for the panel. Its paragraph on notes now describes the new rule and the open-drawer wording, and its example panel shows a reviewing note.

files.note: Replaces the old notes test with one that reads each row's notes by title, closed and open, and updates the drawer test for the new failing · clean notes.

checks.text: Removing the reviewing label from the notes in notesOf leaves all 234 tests passing, so no test checks that note or its orange claude color. A test row with a hold and a reviewing label would cover it. Checked by making that change at this head and running claude plugin test.
The helper takes the Text after a title as that row's notes, unless it is empty or looks like an age such as 5m, in which case the row has no notes.

files.note: Describes which notes a row shows, the open-drawer wording, and that no note names conflict.

checks.text: The paragraph matches notesOf: the order, the colors, the open-drawer phrases, and the rule that no note names conflict. The example's lines still end in one column. Checked by reading both against the head.
